L29: #### Paper 2021/221
L30: 
L31: ### 【17†The Direction of Updatable Encryption Does Matter】
L32: 
L33: Ryo Nishimaki, NTT Social Informatics Laboratories
L34: ##### Abstract
L35: We introduce a new definition for key updates, called backward-leak uni-directional key updates, in updatable encryption (UE). This notion is a variant of uni-directional key updates for UE. We show that existing secure UE schemes in the bi-directional key updates setting are not secure in the backward-leak uni-directional key updates setting. Thus, security in the backward-leak uni-directional key updates setting is strictly stronger than security in the bi-directional key updates setting.
L36: This result is in sharp contrast to the equivalence theorem by Jiang (Asiacrypt 2020), which says security in the bi-directional key updates setting is equivalent to security in the existing uni-directional key updates setting. We call the existing uni-directional key updates ``forward-leak uni-directional'' key updates to distinguish two types of uni-directional key updates in this paper.
L37: We also present a UE scheme that is secure in the backward-leak uni-directional key updates setting under the learning with errors assumption.
L38: Note: Retracted the obfuscation-based construction. (2024/4/18) Publication information and presentation improvement. (12/21/2021) Fixing a minor issue in definitions. (11/25/2021) The presentation was improved. (9/16/2021)

L50@P2: iii
L51@P2: Introduction
L52@P2: FrodoKEM is a family of IND-CCA2 secure key-encapsulation mechanisms (KEMs) that were designed to
L53@P2: be conservative yet practical post-quantum constructions. The security of FrodoKEM derives from
L54@P2: cautious parameterizations of the well-studied learning with errors (LWE) problem, which in turn has
L55@P2: close connections to conjectured-hard problems on generic, “algebraically unstructured” lattices.
L56@P2: The core building block of FrodoKEM is a public-key encryption scheme called FrodoPKE, whose INDCPA security is tightly related to the hardness of a corresponding learning with errors problem.
L57@P2: As a key encapsulation mechanism, FrodoKEM is a two-pass protocol that allows two parties to derive a
L58@P2: shared secret. This shared secret can then be used to establish a secure communication channel using a
L59@P2: symmetric-key algorithm such as AES.
L60@P2: FrodoKEM is parameterized by the pseudorandom generator (𝑃𝑅𝐺) that is used for the generation of a
L61@P2: matrix called A. This document considers two main variants, which are determined by the use of either
L62@P2: AES128 [FIPS197] or SHAKE128 [FIPS202] for the generation of A.
L63@P2: In addition, FrodoKEM consists of two main variants: a “standard” variant that does not impose any
L64@P2: restriction on the reuse of key pairs (i.e., it is suitable for applications in which a large number of
L65@P2: ciphertexts may be encrypted to a single public key), and an “ephemeral” variant that is suitable for
L66@P2: applications in which the number of ciphertexts produced relative to any single public key is fairly small.
L67@P2: Concretely, this document specifies the following FrodoKEM schemes or parameter sets targeting three
L68@P2: security levels:
L69@P2: - FrodoKEM-640-〈𝑃𝑅𝐺〉 and eFrodoKEM-640-〈𝑃𝑅𝐺〉, which match or exceed the brute-force
L70@P2: security of AES128.
L71@P2: - FrodoKEM-976-〈𝑃𝑅𝐺〉 and eFrodoKEM-976-〈𝑃𝑅𝐺〉, which match or exceed the brute-force
L72@P2: security of AES192.
L73@P2: - FrodoKEM-1344-〈𝑃𝑅𝐺〉 and eFrodoKEM-1344-〈𝑃𝑅𝐺〉, which match or exceed the brute-force
L74@P2: security of AES256.
L75@P2: The schemes above correspond to Levels 1, 3 and 5, respectively, as defined by NIST [NIST-CFP]. The
L76@P2: label “eFrodoKEM” corresponds to the ephemeral variants.
L77@P2: The options for 〈𝑃𝑅𝐺〉 are AES or SHAKE, when either AES128 or SHAKE128 (respectively) is used for
L78@P2: the generation of the matrix A. Thus, the first FrodoKEM variant consists of the schemes FrodoKEM-640-
L79@P2: AES, FrodoKEM-976-AES, and FrodoKEM-1344-AES (and their corresponding ephemeral variants).
L80@P2: Analogously, the second FrodoKEM variant consists of the schemes FrodoKEM-640-SHAKE, FrodoKEM976-SHAKE, and FrodoKEM-1344-SHAKE (and their corresponding ephemeral variants).
L81@P2: For brevity, in some cases this document drops the 𝑃𝑅𝐺 label in the parameter set name to refer
L82@P2: generically to the schemes targeting a certain security level (e.g., the use of FrodoKEM-640 refers to the
L83@P2: Level 1 parameter sets FrodoKEM-640-AES and FrodoKEM-640-SHAKE). Unless explicitly stated, those
L84@P2: names also include the ephemeral variants.
L85@P2: Annex A (informative) details the various parameters defining the FrodoKEM parameter sets. Annex B
L86@P2: (informative) contains the security estimates for the different instantiations according to the analysis
L87@P2: based on the core-SVP hardness. Similarly, Annex C (informative) describes the security estimates
L88@P2: according to a more refined analysis of the cost of cryptanalytic attacks, and Annex D (informative)
L89@P2-4: describes the security estimates derived from the security reductions.FrodoKEM – Preliminary Standardization Proposal

L91@P4: 1 Scope
L92@P4: This document specifies key encapsulation mechanisms from the FrodoKEM family. In particular, it
L93@P4: specifies:
L94@P4: - The process for generating key pairs;
L95@P4: - The process for encapsulation using a public key;
L96@P4: - The process for decapsulation using a secret key and ciphertext.

L104@P4: IND-CPA security

L106@P4: ciphertexts for arbitrary plaintexts

L108@P4: IND-CCA2 security

L110@P4: adaptively-chosen ciphertexts to be decrypted, and then use the results to distinguish a target ciphertext
L111@P4: without consulting the oracle on the challenge ciphertext
